goal.statement: Shorten the time it takes a qualified inbound lead to become a won opportunity, without losing the approval discipline on discounts.
goal.outcome: A sales team that can see where a lead stalls, and an approval gate that still holds at the discount threshold.

metric.name: median_lead_to_won_days
metric.definition: Median calendar days from lead capture to the opportunity reaching the Won stage, over leads captured in the trailing quarter.
metric.target: stated by the business; this plan does not invent one

observedFacts.statement: Every opportunity stage change is recorded with its actor and reason, so the time spent in each stage is derivable without new instrumentation.
observedFacts.source: app inspect: opportunity, opportunity-stage-history; docs/JTBD.md JTBD-05

observedFacts.statement: The discount approval threshold is a versioned, fingerprinted policy rather than a hardcoded branch, so changing it is a new policy version and not a code edit.
No campaign, audience, journey, experiment or attribution record exists in this application.
observedFacts.source: app inspect: resources[]; docs/benchmarks/CRM_JTBD_MATRIX.md, all JTBD-MK rows

derivedMetrics.statement: Median days in each stage, computed from the stage-history rows rather than from any new field.

assumptions.statement: The declared pipeline stage order is the funnel the business means, and a skipped stage is a data problem rather than a second funnel.

inferences.statement: If dwell time concentrates before the approval stage, the approval gate is not what is slowing the funnel, and loosening it would cost discipline for nothing.

recommendations.statement: Publish the dwell-time view first and change nothing else until it has a quarter of data behind it.

unavailableEvidence.statement: The baseline for median_lead_to_won_days cannot be computed for leads captured before pipeline stage history existed.
unavailableEvidence.reason: Stage history begins at M8; earlier rows have no per-stage timestamps, and no backfill would be evidence.

unavailableEvidence.statement: Which channel produced a lead cannot be reported.
unavailableEvidence.reason: No marketing or attribution primitive exists in this application, and inferring one from a record name would be an invention.

decisions.rationale: The stage-history rows already exist, so the funnel view is a configuration of what is displayed, not a new model.
Recording why an opportunity stalled needs one new field on the record that owns the fact. A parallel record to avoid a revision bump would be the wrong shape (ADR-019).
Reminding an owner about a stalled opportunity needs durable scheduled work, which no package can provide and the kernel does not have. That is an ADR discussion, not a step in this solution.
decisions.gap: Durable scheduled work: something that survives a restart and fires later. No installed package provides it, and no package could — a package cannot give the runtime a scheduler.

rejectedRungs.reason: No installed package exposes a schedule, a timer or a due-date sweep as configuration; app inspect lists no such policy or config key.
A declared seam runs inside a request. There is no seam that runs when nobody is calling, which is the whole requirement.
A provider is reached during an action. It cannot originate work, so an integration does not close this gap.
A custom package would have the same problem as rung 2: it can declare records and actions, but nothing in the package contract wakes it up.

steps.description: Show median dwell time per stage on the opportunity board, next to a data-quality note stating how many rows have complete stage history.
Add a bounded stall-reason field to the opportunity record at a new manifest revision, written only through the existing stage-change action.

checks: the full verification suite passes from a clean clone
the b2b lead-qualification starter installs into an empty project
the dwell-time view states its data-quality caveat on the screen, not only in this plan
the record revision bump is applied through the module factory, with its state file checked in

artifacts.description: The opportunity board gains a per-stage median dwell column and the data-quality note beside it.
The opportunity manifest at its next revision, with the bounded stall-reason field.
Dwell time computed from stage history, including the rows with incomplete history.

limitations.message: The primary metric has no baseline for leads captured before stage history existed, and this plan does not backfill one.
Nothing here reports which channel produced a lead. No marketing or attribution primitive exists.
